{{Short description|Polyhedron with 104 faces}}
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform polyhedron stat table|Sided}}
[[File:Snub icosidodecadodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a snub icosidodecadodecahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''snub [[icosidodecadodecahedron]]''' is a [[nonconvex uniform polyhedron]], indexed as U<sub>46</sub>. It has 104 faces (80 [[triangle]]s, 12 [[pentagon]]s, and 12 [[pentagram]]s), 180 edges, and 60 vertices. As the name indicates, it belongs to the family of [[snub polyhedra]].

==Cartesian coordinates==
Let {{tmath|\rho{{=}} }} {{math|{{val|1.324717957244746|end=...}} }} be the real zero of the polynomial {{tmath|x^3-x-1}}. The constant {{tmath|\rho}} is known as the [[plastic ratio]]. Denote by {{tmath|\phi{{=}} }} {{math|{{val|1.618033988749894|end=...}} }} the [[golden ratio]].

Let the point {{tmath|p}} be given by
<math display=block> p=
\begin{pmatrix}
  \rho \\
  (\phi-\rho)/(\rho+1) \\
  (\rho-\phi)/ \rho
\end{pmatrix}
</math>
Let the matrix {{tmath|M}} be given by
<math display=block> M=
\begin{pmatrix}
  1/2 & -\phi/2 & 1/(2\phi) \\
  \phi/2 & 1/(2\phi) & -1/2 \\
  1/(2\phi) & 1/2 & \phi/2
\end{pmatrix}
</math>

<math>M</math> is the rotation around the axis <math>(1, 0, \phi)</math>  by an angle of <math>2\pi/5</math>, counterclockwise. Let the linear transformations <math>T_0, \ldots, T_{11}</math> be the transformations which send a point <math>(x, y, z)</math> to the [[parity of a permutation|even permutations]] of <math>(\pm x, \pm y, \pm z)</math> with an even number of minus signs.
The transformations <math>T_i</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular tetrahedron]]. The transformations <math>T_i M^j</math> <math>(i = 0,\ldots, 11</math>, <math>j = 0,\ldots, 4)</math> constitute the group of rotational symmetries of a [[regular icosahedron]]. Then the 60 points <math>T_i M^j p</math> are the vertices of a snub icosidodecadodecahedron.

The edge length <math> \lambda =2\sqrt{(\rho^5 -\phi^2) \rho^{-5}}</math>, the circumradius equals <math> \sqrt{(\rho^5-\phi^2)(1 +\rho^{-5})},</math> and the midradius <math> \sqrt{\rho^5-\phi^2}.</math> To get a snub icosidodecadodecahedron with unit edge length, divide all above coordinates by {{tmath|\lambda}}.

== Properties ==
The snub icosidodecadodecahedron was among the ten snub polyhedra discovered by [[Harold Scott MacDonald Coxeter|Coxeter]] and [[J. C. P. Miller|Miller]] in the early 1930's, but published only in 1954. Its equation is in Table 4 of ''Uniform polyhedra''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Coxeter |first1=H. S. M. |author1-link=Harold Scott MacDonald Coxeter |last2=Longuet-Higgins |first2=M. S. |author2-link=Michael S. Longuet-Higgins |last3=Miller |first3=J. C. P. |author3-link=J. C. P. Miller |title=Uniform polyhedra |jstor=91532 |mr=0062446 |year=1954 |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences |issn=0080-4614 |volume=246 |issue=916 |pages=401–450 |publisher=The Royal Society |doi=10.1098/rsta.1954.0003 |bibcode=1954RSPTA.246..401C |s2cid=202575183}}</ref>

The measures listed on David McCooey's {{plainlink |url=https://dmccooey.com/polyhedra/index.html |name=Visual Polyhedra}} can be written in terms of {{tmath|\sqrt{5} }} and plastic constant {{tmath|\rho}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dmccooey.com/polyhedra/SnubIcosidodecadodecahedron.html |title=Snub Icosidodecadodecahedron |last=McCooey |first=David |website=Visual Polyhedra |access-date=16 June 2026}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable" id="types"
|+ The snub icosidodecadodecahedron of unit edge length
! element !! size
|-
| circumscribed radius || <math> R =\tfrac12 \sqrt{\rho^5 +1}</math>
|-
| midscribed radius || <math> r =\tfrac12 \sqrt{\rho^5}</math>
|-
| pentagon center radius || <math> r_5 =\tfrac12 \sqrt{\rho^4 -\tfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} }</math>
|-
| triangle center radius || <math> r_3 =\tfrac12 \sqrt{\rho^5 -\tfrac13 }</math>
|-
| pentagram center radius || <math> r_{\tfrac53} =-\tfrac12 \sqrt{\rho^4 +\tfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} }</math>
|-
| triangle-triangle angle || <math> \alpha_{33} =\arccos\left( \tfrac13 (1 -2\rho^2) \right)</math>
|-
| pentagram-triangle angle || <math> \alpha_{\tfrac53 3} =\arccos\left( \sqrt{\tfrac13 (u -v)} \right)</math>
|-
| pentagon-triangle angle || <math> \alpha_{53} =\arccos\left( -\sqrt{\tfrac13 (u +v)} \right)</math>
|}
With <math> u =2\rho^2 -2\rho +1,</math> <math> v =(\rho^2 -3\rho +1) \tfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}.</math>

McCooey's metrics panel gives volume {{math|4.620684...}}, but no formula. However, {{plainlink |url=https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4766887/geometric-properties-of-snub-icosidodecadodecahedron-and-medial-hexagonal-hexeco |name=this solution}} (see Answer) is correct.

== Graph ==
The [[Skeleton (topology)|skeleton]] of a snub icosidodecadodecahedron can be represented as a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] with 60 [[Vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] and 180 edges, an [[Eulerian path|Eulerian graph]].<ref>{{mathworld |id=SnubIcosidodecadodecahedralGraph |title=Snub Icosidodecadodecahedral Graph}}</ref>

== Related polyhedra ==
=== Medial hexagonal hexecontahedron===
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform dual polyhedron stat table|Sided}}
The [[medial hexagonal hexecontahedron]] is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] snub icosidodecadodecahedron.
